reason: The cited evidence does not support the key premises. E1 shows twin formation in nickel (not the HEA) due to dislocation climb in the HEA coating, and only at 300 K, not high temperature. E2 shows better wear resistance for fine-grained CoCrFeMnNi, a different HEA, but does not mention twin-mediated plasticity. No evidence links grain refinement to enhanced twinning in FeNiCrCoCu or to reduced wear via this mechanism at high temperature.
premises: Grain refinement in FeNiCrCoCu promotes twin formation during high-temperature deformation
Twin formation accommodates plastic strain and reduces localized deformation and wear
Refined grains lower the activation barrier for twin nucleation at high temperature
Grain refinement in HEAs improves wear resistance under sliding conditions
Dislocation climb in FeNiCrCoCu promotes twin formation in the adjacent material
